t2i_prompt: A 1440 px wide desktop web section as a flat straight-on UI mockup in Swiss International Typographic Style. A thin top bar with a mono uppercase label, then a full-width deep navy band with a large light-weight sans headline. Below, a strict grid of square-cornered tiles alternating deep navy and warm limestone, one column per step of <CONTENT>: a huge light numeral with a slash on top, a short name and one-line note beneath. One tile replaces its numeral with a white blueprint pipe route with flow arrows on navy. Hairline grid lines, flat fills, no shadows.
signature_idea: C&Q stages as a Swiss poster row of slash-numbered tiles, with one stage's numeral swapped for a blueprint of the pipe route it checks.
strengths: almost verbatim brand: navy/limestone, light headline, huge light numerals, square corners
stage order reads left to right at a glance
blueprint tile adds equipment context without clutter
maps directly to the existing Swiss tile grid component
weaknesses: stage text is garbled: '05/ PQ & Review' and '06/ Performance qualification' duplicate the same line
fifth column is cramped and stacks two stages, breaking the even row
03/ moved into the text tile while 03's numeral tile holds the drawing, which confuses the numbering
blueprint pipe drawing is generic and not tied to IQ
brand_fit_why: Navy and limestone tiles, huge light slash numerals, a light headline, hairlines and one blueprint tile are the brand system almost exactly; only the garbled text lets it down.
